The current L01–L04 pages are text and mathematics prototypes. Do not treat them as complete lecture packages until the visual and activity items below are selected, sourced, credited, and tested.

## L01

- Three-stage modeling diagram: problem → mathematical model → numerical model/software → result and interpretation.
- One restrained comic or sketch for the complexity/fitness-for-purpose trade-off.
- Roberts-Austen diffusion profile or historical apparatus, with reuse permission checked.
- Materials Genome Initiative / Materials Project visual.
- One modern ML materials-screening visual, with the claim tied to its paper.
- Titan pressure-hull geometry and one investigation/FEA figure.
- Fast16 normal-versus-tampered EOS/stress curve from the Symantec analysis; verify reuse terms.
- Error-source map aligned with the modeling stages.
- Buffon's needle geometry plus the browser notebook.

## L02

- Shared Buffon notebook from L01 with CSV export.
- Wooclap comparison poll.
- One visual for each of the four π methods.
- Error-versus-$N$ plot in linear and log--log views.
- Plot showing stochastic spread for repeated Buffon runs.
- Large-$N$ polygon plot showing initial convergence and later round-off growth.
- Pair-programming Basel scaffold.

## L03

- Historical analog-computer photograph or diagram with credit.
- Decimal-versus-binary place-value diagram.
- IEEE 754 sign/exponent/fraction diagram for binary32 and binary64.
- Interactive integer/fraction conversion activity.
- Float16/32/64 representation comparison.
- Shared-increment random-walk accumulation plot.
- Exact-integer threshold demonstration.
- Polygon cancellation visualization carried forward from L02.

## L04

- Molab launch instructions and final activity link.
- Runtime-versus-$N$ benchmark for the Python loop.
- Array/vectorization diagram that does not imply automatic parallelism.
- Memory estimate and batching diagram.
- First-call versus reused JIT timing.
- Serial versus parallel CPU comparison.
- CPU/GPU crossover plot, including dtype and hardware.
- Final time–memory–accuracy comparison table populated from measured results.

## Unit-wide checks

- Every essential image needs alt text and a printable interpretation.
- Every external figure needs a source and license/reuse decision.
- Every live activity needs a static fallback.
- Screenshots should not substitute for equations or numerical data that can be rendered accessibly.
